docs.title: CLOSER Vocabulary Consultation 2026
docs.text:
CLOSER are proposing a revision to its Topic Vocabulary, which can be found at: https://ucldata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CLOS/pages/37323020/Topics

The Topic Vocabulary plays an important part in providing a consistent way of searching across our studies. The current vocabulary was developed over 10 years ago to support a smaller set of studies and a smaller range of subject areas. The revision is driven by a number of considerations:

  • Improving consistency
  • Alignment with the European Language Social Science Thesaurus ELSST
  • Better definitions and examples to assist in classification to the correct topic
  • Addition of what it is not
  • Reorganisation to provide better clarity for discovery
  • To retain a similar number of overall categories for ease of use
  • To provide an improved framework for AI / Machine Learning assisted coding

docs.title: Topic mapping principles
docs.text:
• A question/variable can only be mapped to one topic.
  • A question/variable should only be mapped to a level 1 topic if there isn’t a suitable level 2 topic.
  • If a question/variable overlaps several level 2 topics, it should be mapped to the overarching level 1 topic.
  • All questions/variables from a standardised scale should be mapped to the same topic. If it doesn’t make sense to map them all to a level 2 topic, map them to the overarching level 1 topic (often, but not always, “Mental health (104)”).
  • The population or universe should not be taken into account when mapping a question/variable to a topic. For example, a question asking about smoking during pregnancy should be mapped to “Smoking (10604)” rather than “Pregnancy (114)”, as people who are or have been pregnant are the population rather than the topic.

docs.title: Mental health (104)
docs.text:
Topic Description Definition Terms (ELSST) What it is What it isn’t Examples Changes 104 Mental health APA: a state of mind characterized by emotional well-being, good behavioral adjustment, relative freedom from anxiety and disabling symptoms, and a capacity to establish constructive relationships and cope with the ordinary demands and stresses of life. See also flourishing; normality.1 MENTAL HEALTH Anything related to mental health…Standardised scales measuring general mental health, that aren’t measuring a specific mental illness (e.g. the SDQ). ...that isn't a mental illness, emotion, or wellbeing. For each statement, please tell us how you have been feeling or acting in the past two weeks. I did everything wrongIn the past week, have you thought of killing yourself?Thinking about now, in general would you say your mental health is… Renamed from Mental Health and mental processes 10401 Mental illness APA (mental disorder): any condition characterized by cognitive and emotional disturbances, abnormal behaviors, impaired functioning, or any combination of these. Such disorders cannot be accounted for solely by environmental circumstances and may involve physiological, genetic, chemical, social, and other factors. Specific classifications of mental disorders are elaborated in the American Psychiatric Association’s Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (see DSM–IV–TR; DSM–5) and the World Health Organization’s International Classification of Diseases. Also called mental illness; psychiatric disorder; psychiatric illness; psychological disorder. See also psychopathology.2 MENTALLY ILLMENTAL DISORDERSPSYCHOPATHOLOGYPSYCHIATRYPSYCHOTIC DISORDERS A diagnosable mental illness (e.g. depression, schizophrenia, anorexia nervosa).Standardised scales measuring a diagnosable mental illness (e.g. the CES-D, the EPDS, the GAD-7, the MFQ, the PHQ-9). Emotions that could be related to mental illnesses (e.g. sadness) should be tagged to "Emotions (10404)". Have you ever had any of the following problems: anorexia nervosaDo these specific problem(s) apply to this child? Mental illness / depressionWhich seems worse, the depression or the anxiety? (use subject's own terms) Renamed from Mental disorders 10403 Wellbeing APA: a state of happiness and contentment, with low levels of distress, overall good physical and mental health and outlook, or good quality of life.3 WELL-BEING (HEALTH)WELL-BEING (SOCIETY)PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING Positive psychological functioning and the positive aspects of mental health (e.g. happiness, life satisfaction, quality of life, contentment).Standardised scales measuring mental wellbeing (e.g. the WEMWBS). Indicators of mental illness (e.g. sadness, anxiety). All things considered how satisfied or dissatisfied are you with your life as a whole?These questions are about how you feel and how things have been with you during the past 4 weeks. For each question, please give the one answer that comes closest to the way you have been feeling. How much time during the past four weeks… Have you been a happy person?How much of the time during the past 4 weeks have you felt calm and peaceful? 10404 Emotions APA: a complex reaction pattern, involving experiential, behavioral, and physiological elements, by which an individual attempts to deal with a personally significant matter or event. The specific quality of the emotion (e.g., fear, shame) is determined by the specific significance of the event. For example, if the significance involves threat, fear is likely to be generated; if the significance involves disapproval from another, shame is likely to be generated. Emotion typically involves feeling but differs from feeling in having an overt or implicit engagement with the world."4 EMOTIONAL STATESEMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT Standardised scales measuring emotions (e.g. the UCLA loneliness scale). Emotions related to wellbeing (e.g. happiness, contentment) should be tagged to "Wellbeing (10403)". In the past week have you had a spell of feeling sad, miserable or depressed?How often do you feel emotionally or mentally exhausted at the end of the day?I feel tense or ‘wound up’

Note: For standardised scales measuring mental health, tag all the questions in the scale to the overall topic the scale is measuring (e.g. if the scale is measuring depression, tag all questions to mental illness; if the scale is measuring wellbeing, tag all questions to wellbeing). Do not tag questions in the scale to different topics.

docs.title: Personality (118)
docs.text: Topic Description Definition Terms (ELSST) What it is What it isn’t Examples Changes 118 Personality APA: the enduring configuration of characteristics and behavior that comprises an individual’s unique adjustment to life, including major traits, interests, drives, values, self-concept, abilities, and emotional patterns. Personality is generally viewed as a complex, dynamic integration or totality shaped by many forces, including hereditary and constitutional tendencies; physical maturation; early training; identification with significant individuals and groups; culturally conditioned values and roles; and critical experiences and relationships. Various theories explain the structure and development of personality in different ways, but all agree that personality helps determine behavior. See also personality development; personality psychology; personality structure.<sup>1</sup> PERSONALITYPERSONALITY DEVELOPMENTPERSONALITY DISORDERSHUMAN NATUREPERSONALITY TRAITS Personality is who you are. Some aspects can change over time and be shaped by the environment and/or experiences (e.g. personal values). Please choose the number which best describes how you see yourself, using a scale from 1 to 7 where 1 means 'does not apply to me at all' and 7 means 'applies to me perfectly'.I see myself as someone who is relaxed, handles stress well.He can be coaxed out of a forbidden activityHas anyone ever thought there might be a problem with her behaviour or personality?
